title: Understanding the Difference Between Plot and Story
summary: The creator explains the difference between plot and story, referencing Guillermo Del Toro's definition that plot is rhythm and story is melody. The main lesson is that understanding the distinction between the objective plot events and the subjective story themes helps clarify discussions about films and narratives.
key_points: The creator uses Guillermo Del Toro's definition: plot is rhythm and story is melody.
Plot is the heartbeat of the story, the drumbeat, and the A to B to C sequence of what happens and why.
Story is internal, abstract, emotional, and thematic.
People often get confused about motifs, and because stories are abstract, they are open to different subjective readings.
The creator claims James Cameron's Avatar is a masturbatory white man's colonial power fantasy, which is a reading of the story rather than what was intended.
In Breaking Bad, Skyler White is antagonistic to the protagonist, but the creator claims she is unequivocally not the villain; Walter is the villain.
Brian Cranston couldn't fathom why Frankie Muniz hated Skyler because Cranston understands the story.
The creator claims that arguments about a story's meaning must be based in the plot.
People who say "it's not that deep" usually do not understand the relationship between story and plot.
content:
let’s see if my hyperbolic hook makes people mad again #story #plot #writing #film #movies

You don't understand plot versus story. And for those of you that do, stick around. I want this video to be a resource for you to send to other people when you're getting into arguments with people who also don't understand plot versus story, let me be a conduit for you through which you can call other people stupid on the internet. But what was really frustrating about this is that these two words are used so interchangeably that depending on where you're taught and by who, you could be taught the same things with the words flipped. For sake of argument, I'm using Guillermo Del Toro's [citation needed idk where i read this]* definition that plot is rhythm and story is melody. What do I mean by that? The plot is the heartbeat of the story. It is the drum beat to which story keeps time to. It is A to B to C to D, what happens and why? The story is the internal, it is the abstract, it is the emotional, and it is the thematic. More specifically, when a lot of people get tripped up about plot versus story is when they get confused about the motifs that a story is trying to convey. And because a story is more abstract, people can have different readings of it. And different readings of the motifs of a story can change how the plot points are viewed. For example, I'm on record for saying that James Cameron's Avatar is a masturbatory white man's colonial power fantasy. Do I think that's the story that he was trying to tell? No, but I think that's the story he told because the reading of a story is where we get into into the subjective*. Another example I think of all the time is Skyler White. Everyone was so quick to jump down Skyler White's throat and frame her as the villain of the entire story. And while she certainly is antagonistic at times, being in opposition to our protagonist, she is most certainly not the villain. That is unequivocally Walter. But case in point, there was that whole conversation that Brian Cranston had with Frankie Muniz, in which Frankie Muniz was like, "I hated Skyler." And he went, "let me get this straight. Walter does all these other things, but you still hate her?" The reason Brian Cranston couldn't fathom why someone would think this is because he understands the story. And as much as I champion the death of the author, there are just some incorrect readings of a story. But in the same way that we argue our opinions by basing them in fact, do we argue our readings of a story by basing it in the plot? And by extension, the people who say "it's not that deep" when you're talking to them about a story are the people that don't think to look [past]* the plot. So if you're ever in an argument with some blockhead who just won't understand the points that you're making, it's 99% of the time because they don't understand the relationship between story and plot. In which case send them this video and I will call them stupid for you. Stupid.
